=== run_burst.sbatch ===
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=flits-fit
#SBATCH --partition=expansion
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=16
#SBATCH --mem=32G
#SBATCH --time=00:30:00
#SBATCH --output=/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs/logs/%x_%j.out
#SBATCH --error=/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs/logs/%x_%j.err

# Usage: sbatch --job-name=<burst> run_burst.sbatch <config.yaml>
set -euo pipefail
CONFIG="${1:?pass a config yaml as arg 1}"

# Pin BLAS to 1 thread/process: the dynesty pool runs <cpus-per-task> python
# workers; without this each spawns its own BLAS pool and oversubscribes the
# node (256 threads on 16 cores), which silently inflates wall time.
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
export OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1
export MKL_NUM_THREADS=1
export NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=1

source /home/jfaber/flits/venv/bin/activate
cd /home/jfaber/flits/dsa110-FLITS

echo "[$(date)] node=$(hostname) cpus=${SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK} config=${CONFIG}"
python -u scattering/scripts/run_scattering_analysis.py "${CONFIG}"
echo "[$(date)] done rc=$?"

# Modular SSH config. Per-host blocks live in ~/.ssh/config.d/*.conf
=== known hpcc host refs ===
#!/bin/bash
# Runs ON the HPCC login node (inside tmux). Flicker-free squeue + recent sacct.
INTERVAL=${1:-8}
trap 'printf "\033[?25h\n[queue watch stopped]\n"; exit 0' INT
printf '\033[2J\033[?25l'
while true; do
  frame=$(
    printf '\033[1;36m== QUEUE  %s ==\033[0m\n' "$(date '+%H:%M:%S')"
    squeue -u "$USER" -o '%.10i %.16j %.9P %.8T %.9M %.6C %R' 2>/dev/null
    printf '\n\033[1;36m== recent jobs (sacct, today) ==\033[0m\n'
    sacct -u "$USER" -X --starttime today \
      --format=JobID,JobName%16,State,Elapsed,NCPUS,MaxRSS -P 2>/dev/null \
      | tail -6 | column -t -s'|'
  )
  printf '\033[H'; printf '%s\n' "$frame" | sed $'s/$/\033[K/'; printf '\033[J'
  sleep "$INTERVAL"
done

=== run_joint.sbatch ===
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=flits-joint
#SBATCH --partition=expansion
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
#SBATCH --mem=16G
#SBATCH --time=00:30:00
#SBATCH --output=/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs/logs/%x_%j.out
#SBATCH --error=/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs/logs/%x_%j.err
set -euo pipefail
BURST="${1:?pass a burst name}"
NLIVE="${2:-600}"
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=1
source /home/jfaber/flits/venv/bin/activate
cd /home/jfaber/flits/dsa110-FLITS/scattering
NPROC="${SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK:-8}"   # pool size tracks the core allocation
echo "[$(date)] node=$(hostname) joint burst=${BURST} nlive=${NLIVE} nproc=${NPROC} extra=${*:3}"
python -u /central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs/run_joint_fit.py "${BURST}" "${NLIVE}" "${NPROC}" "${@:3}"
echo "[$(date)] done rc=$?"

  "content": "import json, glob, re, os, math\nfrom collections import defaultdict\n\nrows = []\nfor f in glob.glob(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), \"*_joint_fit*.json\")):\n    d = json.load(open(f))\n    name = os.path.basename(f)[: -len(\"_joint_fit*.json\") + len(\"*.json\") - 5]\n    b = d.get(\"burst\", \"?\")\n    # parse tag from filename\n    m = re.match(r\"(.+?)_joint_fit(.*)\\.json\", os.path.basename(f))\n    tag = m.group(2).lstrip(\"_\") if m else \"\"\n    a = d.get(\"alpha\", {})\n    t = d.get(\"tau_1ghz\", {})\n    lo, hi = (d.get(\"alpha_bounds\") or [None, None])\n    amed = a.get(\"median\")\n    aep, aem = a.get(\"err_plus\"), a.get(\"err_minus\")\n    railed = \"\"\n    if amed is not None and lo is not None:\n        if amed - lo < 0.02:\n            railed = \"RAIL_LO\"\n        elif hi - amed < 0.02:\n            railed = \"RAIL_HI\"\n    rows.append(dict(\n        burst=b, tag=tag or \"(base)\",\n        C=d.get(\"components_C\"), D=d.get(\"components_D\"),\n        s2=d.get(\"gain_s2\"),\n        alpha=amed, aep=aep, aem=aem,\n        tau=t.get(\"median\"), tep=t.get(\"err_plus\"), tem=t.get(\"err_minus\"),\n        lnZ=d.get(\"log_evidence\"), lnZe=d.get(\"log_evidence_err\"),\n        railed=railed,\n    ))\n\nbursts = defaultdict(list)\nfor r in rows:\n    bursts[r[\"burst\"]].append(r)\n\ndef fz(x, n=3):\n    return f\"{x:.{n}f}\" if isinstance(x, (int, float)) else str(x)\n\nfor b in sorted(bursts):\n    rs = bursts[b]\n    rs.sort(key=lambda r: (-(r[\"lnZ\"] or -9e9)))\n    best = rs[0][\"lnZ\"]\n    print(f\"\\n===== {b}  (best lnZ ranked; ΔlnZ vs best) =====\")\n    print(f\"{'tag':24} {'C/D':5} {'s2':5} {'alpha':>16} {'tau_ms':>14} {'lnZ':>12} {'ΔlnZ':>9}  flag\")\n    for r in rs:\n        cd = f\"{r['C']}/{r['D']}\" if r[\"C\"] else \"-\"\n        s2 = \"\" if r[\"s2\"] is None else str(r[\"s2\"])\n        al = f\"{fz(r['alpha'])}+{fz(r['aep'],3)}/-{fz(r['aem'],3)}\" if r[\"alpha\"] is not None else \"-\"\n        ta = f\"{fz(r['tau'],4)}\" if r[\"tau\"] is not None else \"-\"\n        dz = (r[\"lnZ\"] - best) if r[\"lnZ\"] is not None else None\n        print(f\"{r['tag']:24} {cd:5} {s2:5} {al:>16} {ta:>14} {fz(r['lnZ'],1):>12} {fz(dz,1):>9}  {r['railed']}\")\n"

`s2` is the gain-prior variance: **profiled-s2 lnZ is empirical-Bayes (not comparable across component count N); the fixed-s2 ladder is the clean cross-N Bayes factor.** So component verdicts must come from the fixed-s2 grids. Computing the sign-flip test:

> TOOL

```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/jakobfaber/Developer/repos/github.com/jakobtfaber/dsa110-FLITS/analysis/scattering-refit-2026-06/joint_ladder/_s2verdict.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Fixed-s2 cross-N Bayes factor: is the extra component real?\n\nProfiled-s2 lnZ is an empirical-Bayes (profile) Z and is NOT comparable across\ncomponent count N. Only the fixed-s2 ladder gives a clean cross-N Bayes factor.\nA component is statistically real only if ΔlnZ(N+1 vs N) is consistently\npositive (>~5) across ALL s2 values; a sign flip with the prior scale means the\nextra component is prior-driven, not data-driven.\n\"\"\"\nimport json, glob, os, re\nfrom collections import defaultdict\n\nD = os.path.dirname(__file__)\nrecs = {}\nfor f in glob.glob(os.path.join(D, \"*_joint_fit*.json\")):\n    d = json.load(open(f))\n    m = re.match(r\"(.+?)_joint_fit_(.*)\\.json\", os.path.basename(f))\n    if not m:\n        continue\n    burst, tag = m.group(1), m.group(2)\n    recs[(burst, tag)] = (d.get(\"log_evidence\"), (d.get(\"alpha\") or {}).get(\"median\"))\n\n# group by burst, find s2 grids and the C/D pairs that differ by one component\ns2vals = [1, 10, 100]\nbursts = sorted({b for (b, _) in recs})\nfor b in bursts:\n    tags = [t for (bb, t) in recs if bb == b]\n    s2tags = [t for t in tags if \"_s2-\" in t]\n    if not s2tags:\n        continue\n    # base config (CxDy) -> dict of s2 -> lnZ\n    grids = defaultdict(dict)\n    for t in s2tags:\n        base, s2 = t.split(\"_s2-\")\n        grids[base][int(s2)] = recs[(b, t)]\n    bases = sorted(grids)\n    print(f\"\\n===== {b} : fixed-s2 cross-N test =====\")\n    for base in bases:\n        line = f\"  {base:6}\"\n        for s in s2vals:\n            v = grids[base].get(s)\n            line += f\"  s2={s:<3} lnZ={v[0]:.1f}\" if v else f\"  s2={s:<3} --      \"\n        print(line)\n    # pairwise: for configs differing by exactly one component (C+1 or D+1)\n    def cd(base):\n        mm = re.match(r\"C(\\d+)D(\\d+)\", base)\n        return (int(mm.group(1)), int(mm.group(2)))\n    for i, a in enumerate(bases):\n        for bb in bases:\n            ca, da = cd(a); cb, db = cd(bb)\n            if (cb == ca + 1 and db == da) or (db == da + 1 and cb == ca):\n                deltas = []\n                for s in s2vals:\n                    va, vb = grids[a].get(s), grids[bb].get(s)\n                    if va and vb:\n                        deltas.append(vb[0] - va[0])\n                if deltas:\n                    signs = {(\"+\" if x > 0 else \"-\") for x in deltas}\n                    verdict = \"REAL (consistent +)\" if all(x > 5 for x in deltas) else (\n                        \"NOT robust (sign flips)\" if len(signs) > 1 else \"weak/consistent-neg\")\n                    ds = \" / \".join(f\"{x:+.1f}\" for x in deltas)\n                    print(f\"    Δ({bb} vs {a}) across s2: {ds}   -> {verdict}\")\n"
}

Acronyms:
CHIME — Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment  
DSA — Deep Synoptic Array  
FRB — Fast Radio Burst  

I recomputed from the raw files under [joint_ladder](/Users/jakobfaber/Developer/repos/github.com/jakobtfaber/dsa110-FLITS/analysis/scattering-refit-2026-06/joint_ladder/LADDER_SUMMARY.md:1). Verdict: most of the numerical claims survive, but two conclusions are weaker than written: `oran`’s extra-component claim is only supported by profiled-s2 evidence in this directory, and base-vs-shared-zeta evidence comparability is not as clean as the summary implies.

**CLAIM 1 — PARTIAL.**  
Confirmed that component-family lnZ and base/shared-zeta lnZ are on radically different scales: base/shared-zeta ranges are negative, while component rows are positive. Examples: `whitney` base `-11686.585`, shared-zeta `-10882.255`, C1D1 `+23888.159`; `johndoeII` base `-1993.442`, shared-zeta `-2006.789`, C1D1 `+5948.690`. Do not subtract across those.

I did not find the PASS table secretly choosing a CxDy model by comparing it against base/shared-zeta. But the “casey/chromatica/freya/wilhelm sharedzeta choice is same-family/comparable” claim is only partly defensible. The JSON metadata and [fit selector](/Users/jakobfaber/Developer/repos/github.com/jakobtfaber/dsa110-FLITS/scattering/scat_analysis/burstfit_joint.py:940) show base, shared-zeta, and multi-component paths use different likelihood classes and often different alpha priors. For example `casey` base has `alpha_bounds=[1,6]`, `marginalize_gain=true`; shared-zeta has `alpha_bounds=[1.5,6]`, `shared_zeta=true`. So shared-zeta may be scientifically preferable, but treating its lnZ minus base lnZ as a pristine Bayes factor is too strong.

**CLAIM 2 — CONFIRM for the three fixed-s2 tests.**  
The deltas are correctly recomputed:

| burst | test | ΔlnZ s2=1 / 10 / 100 | verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `whitney` | C2D1 − C1D1 | `-5.290 / +1.720 / -4.576` | sign-flip, not real |
| `johndoeII` | C2D2 − C2D1 | `+150.909 / -126.291 / +119.699` | sign-flip, not robust |
| `phineas` | C3D1 − C2D1 | `+1.659 / +6.197 / -1.248` | not robust |

Evidence errors are about `0.45-0.57`, so these sign flips are not numerical noise.

**CLAIM 3 — CONFIRM, but apply it consistently.**  
The railing signature is present: posterior medians only about `1.3-1.5 sigma` above the lower bound, with asymmetric one-sided errors.

Key examples:

| burst/model | alpha | lower bound | `(alpha-lower)/err_minus` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `hamilton` C1D1 | `1.50446 -0.00343/+0.00716` | `1.5` | `1.30` |
| `hamilton` shared-zeta | `1.50437 -0.00334/+0.00697` | `1.5` | `1.31` |
| `whitney` shared-zeta | `1.51448 -0.01062/+0.02153` | `1.5` | `1.36` |
| `whitney` C1D1 | `1.51687 -0.01255/+0.02445` | `1.5` | `1.35` |
| `johndoeII` C1D1 | `1.50409 -0.00312/+0.00649` | `1.5` | `1.31` |
| `johndoeII` C2D1 | `1.57711 -0.05121/+0.07690` | `1.5` | `1.51` |
| `johndoeII` C2D2 | `1.95259 -0.32958/+0.10991` | `1.5` | `1.37` |

That last `johndoeII` C2D2 value is “off the literal rail” but still edge-influenced by this criterion. Also, under the stricter fit-quality contract you provided, alpha below `2.0` is a physics fail, so `johndoeII` should not be promoted to a clean measurement.

**CLAIM 4 — PARTIAL.**  
`hamilton` complete FAIL is solid. Base alpha is `1.00629` with base lower prior `1`, below the physical floor; shared-zeta and all component rows rail near `1.50-1.51`.

`johndoeII` low/unstable is solid, and arguably even more damning than written. Base is `1.05679`; shared-zeta/C1D1 rail; C2D1 is `1.577`; C2D2 is `1.953` but has a lower error of `0.330`, so its 1.5-sigma interval reaches the prior edge. No clean number.

`whitney recoverable` is the weakest part. The base fit is numerically clean in alpha: `3.74749 -0.04383/+0.03256`, tau `1.08951 ms`, base lower prior `1`. The component/shared-zeta path rails at alpha `~1.515-1.519`, tau `~0.491 ms`. That is not just a harmless model-choice difference; it is a factor `~2.22` tau disagreement. I would not call the base alpha “trustworthy” without a model-misspecification explanation and figure review. The defensible wording is: “base gives an in-bounds candidate alpha; shared-zeta/component fits fail; burst requires follow-up before quoting a final alpha.”

**Overstated PASS Risks**  
`isha = MARGINAL` is fair, not too harsh. C2D1 is `alpha=5.38597 -1.94755/+0.50111`, tau `0.01735 ms`; the upper 1.5-sigma interval crosses `6.0`, and the lower tail reaches `~3.44`. MARGINAL is the right label.

`oran` is breakable. The summary says C2D1 gains a second component from `Δ+178 vs C1D1`; I recompute profiled lnZ C2D1 − C1D1 as `25045.367 - 24866.734 = +178.633`. But there are no `oran_*_s2-1/10/100.json` fixed-s2 confirmation files in the ladder. Under the summary’s own rule, “component selection uses fixed-s2 only,” `oran`’s second-component claim is not cleanly established here. Its alpha `2.68768 +/- ~0.16` is in-bounds if C2D1 is accepted, but the component-count conclusion is overstated.

`mahi`, `zach`, and `phineas` selected component rows are internally consistent by profiled evidence, but only the fixed-s2 tests listed above were available for robustness. The strongest actual break I can make is `oran`; the strongest caution is `whitney`.

        type=int,
        default=1,
        help="number of temporal components (sub-pulses) in the DSA band",
    )
    ap.add_argument(
        "--force-multi",
        dest="force_multi",
        action="store_true",
        help="run the multi-component likelihood even at C1D1, so its lnZ "
        "is normalization-matched to C2/D2 runs (model-selection baseline)",
    )
    ap.add_argument(
        "--shared-zeta",
        dest="shared_zeta",
        action="store_true",
        help="ONE frequency-evolving intrinsic width zeta(nu)=zeta_1ghz*nu^x_zeta "
        "shared across both bands (gain-marginal, 8-dim) instead of per-band zeta; "
        "gives a single coherent burst across the full band",
    )
    # Per-band PBF (DEFAULT): CHIME and DSA are separate FRBModel instances, so each
    # carries its own pulse-broadening function. The wilhelm test showed the bands want
    # different shapes -- CHIME mildly prefers a Kolmogorov power-law tail, DSA an
    # exponential -- and CHIME-powerlaw/DSA-exp beats all-exp by dlnZ=+4.0
    # (.agents/experiment-powerlaw-pbf.md). The Kolmogorov default (beta=11/3) is
    # physically motivated, but the +4.0 evidence is wilhelm-only so far; revisit
    # when more bursts carry per-band PBF evidence. Pass --pbf-C exp to revert CHIME
    # to a single global exponential PBF.
    ap.add_argument(
        "--gain-s2",
        dest="gain_s2",
        type=float,
        default=None,
        help="fix the gain-prior variance s2 instead of ML-profiling it per fit. "
        "Profiled s2 (default) gives a profile/empirical-Bayes Z; for a CLEAN "
        "cross-N Bayes factor (component model selection) fix s2 to one value "
        "across the whole ladder. Output is tagged _s2-<val> so it does not "
        "overwrite the profiled run.",
    )
    ap.add_argument("--pbf-C", dest="pbf_C", default="powerlaw", choices=["exp", "powerlaw"])
    ap.add_argument("--pbf-D", dest="pbf_D", default="exp", choices=["exp", "powerlaw"])
    ap.add_argument("--beta-C", dest="beta_C", type=float, default=11.0 / 3.0)
    ap.add_argument("--beta-D", dest="beta_D", type=float, default=11.0 / 3.0)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    multi = a.components_C > 1 or a.components_D > 1 or a.force_multi

    cfg_dir = f"{RUNS}/configs"
    out_dir = f"{RUNS}/data/joint"
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)

    cC = f"{cfg_dir}/{a.burst}_chime_run.yaml"
    cD = f"{cfg_dir}/{a.burst}_dsa_run.yaml"

=== joint_ppc.py (head) ===
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Posterior-predictive per-band check for the joint fits.

Rebuilds each band's FRBModel (same prep as run_joint_fit), evaluates the M3
model at the JOINT best-fit medians, and reports per-band reduced chi2 +
profile overlays. If the joint solution fits BOTH bands well (chi2~1), the
shared tau*nu^-alpha (and its alpha) is a real joint measurement. If one band
is poorly fit, the shallow alpha is a forced compromise between irreconcilable
bands, not a measurement.

  python joint_ppc.py <burst>
"""

import json
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

REPO = os.environ.get("FLITS_REPO", "/home/jfaber/flits/dsa110-FLITS")
RUNS = os.environ.get("FLITS_RUNS", "/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs")
SUF = os.environ.get("FLITS_FIT_SUFFIX", "")  # e.g. "_sharedzeta" to PPC the shared-zeta variant
sys.path.insert(0, f"{REPO}/scattering")
import matplotlib
import yaml

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scat_analysis.burstfit import FRBParams
from scat_analysis.config_utils import load_telescope_block
from scat_analysis.pipeline.io import BurstDataset


def prepare(cfg_path, name, outdir):
    cfg = yaml.safe_load(open(cfg_path))
    tel = load_telescope_block(cfg["telcfg_path"], cfg["telescope"])
    ds = BurstDataset(
        cfg["path"],
        outdir,
        name=name,
        telescope=tel,
        f_factor=int(cfg["f_factor"]),
        t_factor=int(cfg["t_factor"]),
        outer_trim=float(cfg.get("outer_trim", 0.15)),
        onpulse_crop=os.environ.get("FLITS_ONPULSE_CROP", "1") == "1",
        onpulse_pad_factor=float(os.environ.get("FLITS_ONPULSE_PAD", "0.5")),
    )
    m = ds.model
    m.dm_init = float(cfg.get("dm_init", 0.0))
    return m


def band_chi2(model, p, gain=False):
    mod = model(p, "M3")
    if gain:  # apply profiled per-channel gain: model = g_f * K_f
        g = model.gain_spectrum(p, "M3")
        mod = g[:, None] * mod
    noise = np.asarray(model.noise_std, dtype=float)
    if noise.ndim == 1:
        noise = noise[:, None]

=== component_gallery.py ===
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Per-burst component-screening gallery: CHIME | DSA, each a dedispersed
waterfall (freq x time, on-pulse cropped) over its frequency-collapsed profile.
No model overlay -- this is for COUNTING temporal sub-components by eye before
deciding C1 vs C2 fits. Reuses the exact data prep as run_joint_fit/joint_ppc.

  python component_gallery.py <burst>
"""

import os
import sys

import matplotlib
import numpy as np
import yaml

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

REPO = os.environ.get("FLITS_REPO", "/home/jfaber/flits/dsa110-FLITS")
RUNS = os.environ.get("FLITS_RUNS", "/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs")
sys.path.insert(0, f"{REPO}/scattering")
from scat_analysis.config_utils import load_telescope_block
from scat_analysis.pipeline.io import BurstDataset


def prepare(cfg_path, name):
    cfg = yaml.safe_load(open(cfg_path))
    tel = load_telescope_block(cfg["telcfg_path"], cfg["telescope"])
    ds = BurstDataset(
        cfg["path"],
        f"{RUNS}/data/joint",
        name=name,
        telescope=tel,
        f_factor=int(cfg["f_factor"]),
        t_factor=int(cfg["t_factor"]),
        outer_trim=float(cfg.get("outer_trim", 0.15)),
        onpulse_crop=os.environ.get("FLITS_ONPULSE_CROP", "1") == "1",
        onpulse_pad_factor=float(os.environ.get("FLITS_ONPULSE_PAD", "0.5")),
    )
    return ds.model


def panel(axw, axp, m, title):
    d = np.asarray(m.data, float)  # (freq, time), freq ascending
    t = np.asarray(m.time, float)
    # downsample freq for display only if very tall
    step = max(1, d.shape[0] // 512)
    disp = d[::step]
    vmax = np.nanpercentile(disp, 99.5)
    axw.imshow(
        disp,
        aspect="auto",
        origin="lower",
        extent=[t[0], t[-1], 0, d.shape[0]],
        cmap="viridis",
        vmin=np.nanpercentile(disp, 5),
        vmax=vmax,
    )
    axw.set_title(title)
    axw.set_ylabel("freq chan")
    prof = np.nansum(d, axis=0)
    axp.plot(t, prof, "k", lw=0.9)
    axp.axhline(0, color="0.6", lw=0.5)
    axp.set_xlabel("time (ms)")
    axp.set_ylabel("flux (a.u.)")
    axp.margins(x=0)


def main():
    b = sys.argv[1]
    mC = prepare(f"{RUNS}/configs/{b}_chime_run.yaml", f"{b}_chime")
    mD = prepare(f"{RUNS}/configs/{b}_dsa_run.yaml", f"{b}_dsa")
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(13, 6), gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [2, 1]})
    panel(ax[0, 0], ax[1, 0], mC, f"{b}  CHIME (400-800 MHz)")
    panel(ax[0, 1], ax[1, 1], mD, f"{b}  DSA (1.31-1.50 GHz)")
    fig.suptitle(f"{b}: component screen -- count temporal sub-pulses per band", y=1.0)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fp = f"{RUNS}/data/joint/{b}_components.png"
    fig.savefig(fp, dpi=120, bbox_inches="tight")
    print(f"wrote {fp}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

190	def _gain_marginal_multi_band(
191	    model: FRBModel,
192	    params_list: Sequence[FRBParams],
193	    model_keys: Sequence[str],
194	    s2: float | None = None,
195	    eig_rel_floor: float = 1e-6,
196	) -> tuple[float, dict[str, Any]]:
197	    """Per-channel linear-Gaussian gain-marginal evidence for ONE band.
198	
199	    N temporal component kernels K_1..K_N per channel f; the per-component gains
200	    g ~ N(0, s2 I_N) carry the burst spectrum + scintillation. With noise var
201	    sigma_f^2 the per-channel marginal (Gaussian g integrated analytically) is
202	
203	        M_ij = sum_t K_i,t K_j,t          (NxN, per channel)
204	        b_i  = sum_t d_t K_i,t            (N)
205	        S_dd = sum_t d_t^2
206	
207	        ln Z_f = -0.5*[ S_dd/sigma^2 - b^T (M + (sigma^2/s2) I)^-1 b / sigma^2 ]
208	                 - 0.5*T*ln(2 pi sigma^2)                       (FULL data norm)
209	                 - 0.5*ln det( I_N + (s2/sigma^2) M )           (proper Occam)
210	
211	    (The quadratic divisor is sigma^2, not sigma^4 -- verified against the brute
212	    Gaussian evidence d^T Sigma_d^-1 d, Sigma_d = sigma^2 I_T + s2 K K^T, via
213	    Woodbury; the SPEC's sigma^4 was a transcription slip.)
214	
215	    The Occam term GROWS with N and with s2 -- the valid finite-variance penalty
216	    that the flat-improper version (-0.5 ln det M ~ +N ln s2 as s2->inf) got
217	    wrong, rewarding spurious merged components. As s2->inf, ln Z_f reduces to the
218	    flat F-stat profile -0.5*chi2min_f - 0.5*ln det M_f + 0.5*N*ln s2 (the last
219	    is a divergent param-INDEPENDENT constant that cancels in any ln Z DIFFERENCE).
220	
221	    s2 is the gain-prior variance HYPERPARAMETER. If ``s2 is None`` it is profiled
222	    by 1-D ML on a SHARED-per-band value (state in the design notes); pass a float
223	    to fix it. Returns ``(lnZ, diag)`` with diagnostics:
224	    ``frac_culled`` (channels dropped by the eigenvalue guard), ``max_abs_g``
225	    (per component), ``s2``, ``n_supported``.
226	
227	    Eigenvalue conditioning guard: a channel is culled when
228	    min eig(M_f) / max eig(M_f) < ``eig_rel_floor`` (near-degenerate kernels in
229	    the DAMAGE band where two components nearly merge -- M_f singular -> the full-N
230	    solve explodes |g|). A culled-but-SUPPORTED channel (real signal, collinear
231	    kernels) falls back to a rank-1 proper-prior evidence on its top eigenpair --
232	    NOT to the gain=0 baseline -- so a merge stays Occam-penalized (a reward at
233	    large fixed s2 otherwise; see the inline note). Only a genuinely unsupported
234	    channel (emax ~ 0, no signal) gets the gain=0 baseline
235	    -0.5 S_dd/sigma^2 - 0.5 T ln(2 pi sigma^2). ``frac_culled`` counts all
236	    not-full-rank-N channels (rank-1 fallback + unsupported).
237	    """
238	    if model.data is None or model.noise_std is None:
239	        raise RuntimeError("need data + noise_std")
240	    valid = model.valid
241	    if valid is None or not np.any(valid):
242	        return -np.inf, {"frac_culled": 1.0, "max_abs_g": None, "s2": s2, "n_supported": 0}
243	
244	    Ks = np.stack(
245	        [
246	            model(replace(p, c0=1.0, gamma=0.0), mk, freq_subset=valid)
247	            for p, mk in zip(params_list, model_keys)
248	        ]
249	    )  # (N, F, T)
250	    N, F, T = Ks.shape
251	    d = model.data[valid]  # (F, T)
252	    sig = np.clip(model.noise_std[valid], 1e-9, None)  # (F,)
253	    var = sig**2  # (F,)
254	
255	    S_dd = np.einsum("ft,ft->f", d, d)  # (F,)
256	    b = np.einsum("nft,ft->fn", Ks, d)  # (F, N)
257	    M = np.einsum("nft,mft->fnm", Ks, Ks)  # (F, N, N)
258	
259	    # Eigenvalue conditioning guard (per channel). M is symmetric PSD. We keep the
260	    # eigenVECTORS (eigh, not eigvalsh) so a culled channel can fall back to its
261	    # rank-1 top-eigenpair proper evidence instead of the gain=0 baseline -- see
262	    # below for why that distinction is load-bearing.
263	    evals, evecs = np.linalg.eigh(M)  # (F, N) asc, (F, N, N)
264	    emax = evals[:, -1]
265	    emin = evals[:, 0]
266	    supported = emax > 1e-30  # any signal at all
267	    cond_ok = np.zeros(F, dtype=bool)
268	    cond_ok[supported] = (
269	        emin[supported] / np.where(emax[supported] > 0, emax[supported], 1.0) >= eig_rel_floor
270	    )
271	    ok = supported & cond_ok  # well-conditioned channels
272	    # Culled-but-supported channels: kernels collinear (a near-merge), but there
273	    # IS signal. Route them to a rank-1 model on the top eigenvector (one
274	    # effective kernel), NOT to gain=0. This matters because at large fixed s2 the
275	    # gain=0 baseline -0.5 S_dd/var - 0.5 T ln(2pi var) sits ABOVE the proper N=1
276	    # lnZ (which carries the divergent +0.5 ln(s2/var) Occam per channel), so
277	    # culling-to-baseline would REWARD a degenerate merge by ~+0.5 F ln(s2/var)
278	    # (e.g. +676 nats at s2=1e8) -- reintroducing the very bug the prior fixes for
279	    # any caller that bypasses the ordered transform. The rank-1 fallback is
280	    # continuous with the N=1 proper model, so the merge is a penalty, not a reward.
281	    cull = supported & ~cond_ok  # (F,)
282	    eye = np.eye(N)
283	
284	    def _lnZ_at(s2v: float) -> tuple[float, NDArray[np.floating]]:
285	        # gain=0 baseline only for genuinely unsupported (no-signal) channels.
286	        base = -0.5 * S_dd / var - 0.5 * T * np.log(2.0 * np.pi * var)
287	        lnZ_f = base.copy()
288	        g_all = np.zeros((F, N))
289	        if np.any(ok):
290	            Mok = M[ok]  # (G, N, N)
291	            bok = b[ok]  # (G, N)
292	            varok = var[ok]  # (G,)
293	            ridge = (varok / s2v)[:, None, None] * eye[None]
294	            A = Mok + ridge  # (G, N, N)
295	            g = np.linalg.solve(A, bok[:, :, None])[:, :, 0]  # (G, N), the MAP gain
296	            quad = np.einsum("gn,gn->g", g, bok)  # b^T A^-1 b
297	            # ln det( I + (s2/var) M ) via eigvals of M (per channel).
298	            ev_ok = evals[ok]  # (G, N)
299	            logdet_occam = np.sum(
300	                np.log1p((s2v / varok)[:, None] * np.clip(ev_ok, 0.0, None)),
301	                axis=1,
302	            )  # (G,)
303	            lnZ_ok = (
304	                -0.5 * (S_dd[ok] / varok - quad / varok)
305	                - 0.5 * T * np.log(2.0 * np.pi * varok)
306	                - 0.5 * logdet_occam
307	            )
308	            lnZ_f[ok] = lnZ_ok
309	            g_all[ok] = g
310	        if np.any(cull):
311	            # rank-1 proper evidence on the top eigenpair (scalar effective kernel
312	            # with norm^2 = emax, projected data b.v_top). MAP gain along v_top is
313	            # then distributed back onto the components via v_top for diagnostics.
314	            emx = emax[cull]  # (C,)
315	            vtop = evecs[cull][:, :, -1]  # (C, N)
316	            bproj = np.einsum("cn,cn->c", b[cull], vtop)  # (C,)
317	            varc = var[cull]  # (C,)
318	            Ac = emx + varc / s2v
319	            gc = bproj / Ac  # (C,) scalar MAP along v_top
320	            quadc = gc * bproj
321	            occ_c = np.log1p((s2v / varc) * np.clip(emx, 0.0, None))
322	            lnZ_f[cull] = (
323	                -0.5 * (S_dd[cull] / varc - quadc / varc)
324	                - 0.5 * T * np.log(2.0 * np.pi * varc)
325	                - 0.5 * occ_c
326	            )
327	            g_all[cull] = gc[:, None] * vtop  # (C, N)
328	        return float(np.sum(lnZ_f)), g_all
329	
330	    if s2 is None:
331	        # 1-D ML over log s2, range anchored on the data scale: var(ahat) where
332	        # ahat=b/diag(M) is the matched-filter gain ~ sets the signal amplitude.
333	        diagM = np.einsum("fnn->fn", M)
334	        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
335	            ahat = np.where(diagM > 0, b / np.where(diagM > 0, diagM, 1.0), 0.0)
336	        scale = max(float(np.var(ahat[ok])) if np.any(ok) else 1.0, 1e-12)
337	        from scipy.optimize import minimize_scalar
338	
339	        lo, hi = np.log(scale) - 18.0, np.log(scale) + 18.0
340	        res = minimize_scalar(
341	            lambda ls: -_lnZ_at(float(np.exp(ls)))[0],
342	            bounds=(lo, hi),
343	            method="bounded",
344	            options={"xatol": 1e-3},
345	        )
346	        s2_used = float(np.exp(res.x))
347	    else:
348	        s2_used = float(s2)
349	
350	    lnZ, g_all = _lnZ_at(s2_used)
351	    max_abs_g = [float(np.max(np.abs(g_all[:, i]))) if F else 0.0 for i in range(N)]
352	    # NB: n_supported and frac_culled use DIFFERENT denominators. n_supported counts
353	    # only well-conditioned (full-rank-N) channels (`ok`), whereas frac_culled =
354	    # mean(~ok) also counts rank-1-fallback channels as culled -- so in general
355	    # n_supported != (1 - frac_culled) * F.
356	    diag = {
357	        "frac_culled": float(np.mean(~ok)),
358	        "max_abs_g": max_abs_g,
359	        "s2": s2_used,
360	        "n_supported": int(np.count_nonzero(ok)),
361	    }
362	    return (lnZ if np.isfinite(lnZ) else -np.inf), diag
363	
364

def prepare(cfg_path, name, outdir):
    """Rebuild a single band's FRBModel + data-driven init from its run-config."""
    cfg = yaml.safe_load(open(cfg_path))
    tel = load_telescope_block(cfg["telcfg_path"], cfg["telescope"])
    ds = BurstDataset(
        cfg["path"],
        outdir,
        name=name,
        telescope=tel,
        f_factor=int(cfg["f_factor"]),
        t_factor=int(cfg["t_factor"]),
        outer_trim=float(cfg.get("outer_trim", 0.15)),
        onpulse_crop=os.environ.get("FLITS_ONPULSE_CROP", "1") == "1",
        onpulse_pad_factor=float(os.environ.get("FLITS_ONPULSE_PAD", "0.5")),
    )
    model = ds.model
    dm_init = float(cfg.get("dm_init", 0.0))
    model.dm_init = dm_init
    init = data_driven_initial_guess(
        data=model.data,
        freq=model.freq,
        time=model.time,
        dm=dm_init,
        verbose=False,
    ).params
    init = refine_initial_guess_mle(model, init)
    return model, init

bbox_inches=\"tight\")\nprint(f\"wrote {fp}  chime_chi2/pt={RC['chi2']:.3f} dsa_chi2/pt={RD['chi2']:.3f} s2C={RC['s2']:.3g} s2D={RD['s2']:.3g}\")\n"

> AGENT

6 figures sent (all 13 in `joint_ladder/overlays/`). Reviewing the model-vs-data revealed **two verdict changes**, now in the summary:

- **wilhelm: PASS → MARGINAL** — DSA χ²=4.55 (model tracks the high-SNR pulse but shape mismatch is costly >3); α=2.56 is a forced compromise, not clean.
- **whitney: → complete FAIL** — the base α=3.75 isn't a real fit; its model is flat and misses the CHIME multi-peak burst entirely (χ²=2.88). Component path fits but rails. No usable α (Codex's caution was right).

And the failure mechanisms are now visually confirmed:
- **hamilton** — DSA band is essentially **noise**, CHIME one narrow spike → no lever arm → α rails to 1.5.
- The clean winners (zach C2D3, phineas C3D3, mahi, oran, isha) reconstruct correctly: model tracks data, components sit on the sub-peaks.

  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python\n\"\"\"2D (freq x time) joint-fit model vs data: data | model | residual per band.\n\nSame gain-marginal reconstruction as model_overlay.py, but plots the full 2D\npredicted waterfall (sum_n g[f,n] K_n[f,t]) next to the data and the residual,\nso the per-channel spectrum/scint the gains absorb is visible.\n\n  python model_2d.py <burst> <tag>     # tag like C2D3, C4D1\n\"\"\"\nimport json, os, re, sys\nfrom dataclasses import replace\nimport numpy as np\nimport matplotlib\nmatplotlib.use(\"Agg\")\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n\nREPO = os.environ.get(\"FLITS_REPO\", \"/home/jfaber/flits/dsa110-FLITS\")\nRUNS = os.environ.get(\"FLITS_RUNS\", \"/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs\")\nsys.path.insert(0, RUNS)\nsys.path.insert(0, f\"{REPO}/scattering\")\nfrom run_joint_fit import prepare\nfrom scat_analysis.burstfit import FRBParams\nfrom scat_analysis.burstfit_joint import _gain_marginal_multi_band\n\nburst, tag = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]\nmt = re.match(r\"C(\\d+)D(\\d+)\", tag)\nnC, nD = int(mt.group(1)), int(mt.group(2))\nJ = json.load(open(f\"{RUNS}/data/joint/{burst}_joint_fit_{tag}.json\"))\nP = {k: v[\"median\"] for k, v in J[\"percentiles\"].items()}\ntau, alpha = P[\"tau_1ghz\"], P[\"alpha\"]\n\n\ndef band_params(prefix, n, ddm):\n    return [FRBParams(c0=1.0, t0=P[f\"t0_{prefix}{i}\"], gamma=0.0, zeta=P[f\"zeta_{prefix}{i}\"],\n                      tau_1ghz=tau, alpha=alpha, delta_dm=ddm) for i in range(1, n + 1)]\n\n\ndef solve_band(model, ps):\n    valid = model.valid\n    Ks = np.stack([model(replace(p, c0=1.0, gamma=0.0), \"M3\", freq_subset=valid) for p in ps])\n    d = model.data[valid]\n    sig = np.clip(model.noise_std[valid], 1e-9, None)\n    var = sig ** 2\n    b = np.einsum(\"nft,ft->fn\", Ks, d)\n    M = np.einsum(\"nft,mft->fnm\", Ks, Ks)\n    _, diag = _gain_marginal_multi_band(model, ps, [\"M3\"] * len(ps), s2=None)\n    A = M + (var / diag[\"s2\"])[:, None, None] * np.eye(Ks.shape[0])[None]\n    g = np.linalg.solve(A, b[:, :, None])[:, :, 0]\n    pred = np.einsum(\"fn,nft->ft\", g, Ks)\n    resid = (d - pred) / sig[:, None]  # whitened residual\n    chi2 = float(np.sum(resid ** 2) / resid.size)\n    return dict(d=d, pred=pred, resid=resid, t=model.time, f=model.freq[valid], chi2=chi2)\n\n\nRC = solve_band(prepare(f\"{RUNS}/configs/{burst}_chime_run.yaml\", f\"{burst}_chime\", f\"{RUNS}/data/joint\")[0],\n                band_params(\"C\", nC, P.get(\"delta_dm_C\", 0.0)))\nRD = solve_band(prepare(f\"{RUNS}/configs/{burst}_dsa_run.yaml\", f\"{burst}_dsa\", f\"{RUNS}/data/joint\")[0],\n                band_params(\"D\", nD, P.get(\"delta_dm_D\", 0.0)))\n\nfig, ax = plt.subplots(3, 2, figsize=(13, 9))\nfor col, (R, name) in enumerate([(RC, \"CHIME 400-800 MHz\"), (RD, \"DSA 1.31-1.50 GHz\")]):\n    t, f = R[\"t\"], R[\"f\"]\n    ext = [t[0], t[-1], f[0], f[-1]]\n    vmax = np.nanpercentile(R[\"d\"], 99.5)\n    vmin = np.nanpercentile(R[\"d\"], 2)\n    for row, (img, title, cmap, kw) in enumerate([\n        (R[\"d\"], f\"{name}  DATA\", \"viridis\", dict(vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax)),\n        (R[\"pred\"], f\"MODEL ({tag})\", \"viridis\", dict(vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax)),\n        (R[\"resid\"], f\"RESIDUAL (whitened)  χ²/pt={R['chi2']:.2f}\", \"RdBu_r\", dict(vmin=-4, vmax=4)),\n    ]):\n        im = ax[row, col].imshow(img, aspect=\"auto\", origin=\"lower\", extent=ext, cmap=cmap, **kw)\n        ax[row, col].set_title(title, fontsize=9)\n        ax[row, col].set_ylabel(\"freq (GHz)\")\n        fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax[row, col], pad=0.01, fraction=0.04)\n    ax[2, col].set_xlabel(\"time (ms)\")\nfig.suptitle(f\"{burst}  2D joint model {tag} vs data  --  α={alpha:.2f}  τ_1GHz={tau:.3f} ms\", y=1.0)\nfig.tight_layout()\nfp = f\"{RUNS}/data/joint/{burst}_2d_{tag}.png\"\nfig.savefig(fp, dpi=115, bbox_inches=\"tight\")\nprint(f\"wrote {fp}  chime_chi2/pt={RC['chi2']:.3f} dsa_chi2/pt={RD['chi2']:.3f}\")\n"
}

6 sent (all 8 in `joint_ladder/overlays/*_2d_*.png`). These are the full 2D fits: **data | model | whitened residual**, freq×time, per band — the model the likelihood actually operates on.

What they show:
- **zach / phineas / johndoeII** — the 2D model reproduces the frequency-dependent scattering sweep and the per-component spikes; whitened residuals are noise-like (mild structure only at the brightest CHIME pixels).
- **hamilton** — the DSA panel is **pure noise**, model blank there: visually why the joint α has no high-frequency anchor and rails.
- **whitney** — broad multi-peak CHIME vs a clean narrow DSA spike; one τ∝ν^−α can't span both, so α rails to 1.52 while components/gains absorb the rest.
- **isha** — DSA is a broad, weak, low-SNR blob → α unconstrained (the +0.50/−1.95).

Note these reuse the **gain-marginal** reconstruction (per-channel amplitude freedom), so the model absorbs the burst spectrum/scintillation per channel — that's why even railed/failed fits still reproduce the data here; the *parameter* pathology (α) is the failure, not a 2D misfit. The harder misfit test remains the single-profiled-gain `joint_ppc` χ² (what flagged wilhelm/whitney).

> DEVELOPER

How does the game marginal reconstruction work? Is it just a weighting per channel that's imposed after the fit?

> AGENT

Acronyms:
MAP — Maximum A Posteriori (the mode/peak of the posterior)

Short answer: **during the fit it's not a weighting at all — the per-channel amplitudes are integrated out (marginalized). In my figure they're computed after, as the conditional MAP at the median shape — the model's own posterior, not an imposed fudge.**

The mechanics (in `scattering/scat_analysis/burstfit_joint.py:190`, `_gain_marginal_multi_band`):

**In the likelihood.** Each component *n* contributes a fixed-shape kernel `K_n(f,t)` — the scattered sub-pulse at channel *f*, set by that component's `t0_n, zeta_n` and the **shared** `τ·ν^−α` tail (`burstfit_joint.py:246`). The data model per channel is linear in unknown amplitudes:

```
d(f,t) = Σ_n g_{f,n} · K_n(f,t) + noise
```

The `g_{f,n}` (the "gains") are a free amplitude per channel per component = the burst's spectrum × scintillation × component brightness. They get a Gaussian prior `g ~ N(0, s2·I)`. Because the model is linear in `g` and noise is Gaussian, that integral is **analytic** — so at every likelihood call the gains are integrated out and you get a closed-form per-channel marginal evidence (`burstfit_joint.py:207`). The nested sampler therefore only explores the *shape* parameters (`τ, α, t0_n, zeta_n, δDM`); the amplitudes are never sampled. That's the whole point: the shared scattering law is constrained while the per-channel spectrum is free.

**The `s2` and the Occam term.** `s2` is the gain-prior variance — profiled (empirical-Bayes) by default, or fixed for the clean ladder. The `−½ ln det(I + (s2/σ²)M)` term grows with component count, which is the model-selection penalty (and the lever the fixed-s2 sign-flip test probes).

**In my reconstruction (the overlay/2D figures).** Marginalizing destroys the point values, so to *draw* a model I evaluate the gains at their conditional MAP given the median shape — the ridge/Wiener solution (`burstfit_joint.py:295`):

```
g_f = (M_f + (σ²/s2)·I)^−1 b_f ,   model(f,t) = Σ_n g_{f,n} K_n(f,t)
M_ij = Σ_t K_i K_j ,  b_i = Σ_t d_t K_i
```

So yes — the per-channel amplitudes *are* solved after the fit to make the picture, but (a) it's the same linear-Gaussian posterior the fit used, at its mode rather than integrated, and (b) the `(σ²/s2)` ridge is the prior, so they're shrunk, not free least-squares.

The consequence I keep flagging: N free (shrunk) amplitudes per channel give the model lots of room to match each channel, so the 2D model and collapsed profile track the data **by construction** wherever there's signal. The fit's actual constraint lives in the *shared* `τ, α` (one tail law across all channels) and the component count — not in the amplitudes. That's why a railed/failed burst still "looks fit" in these panels; the `joint_ppc` single-profiled-gain χ² is the stricter misfit test.

> AGENT

Confirmed — it's a blanket convention, not tuned. Every burst but casey uses CHIME **f_factor=64 → 16 channels**, t_factor=24; DSA uniformly f_factor=384 → **16 channels**. casey alone uses f_factor=32 (32 channels).

**On the CHIME over-binning — you're right, with a caveat.** α is measured *entirely* from how the tail width scales with frequency, τ(ν)=τ₁GHz·ν^−α. 16 channels = 16 points on that curve across 400–800 MHz — thin leverage, and it also under-samples the scintillation the per-channel gains absorb. So coarser-than-needed binning directly weakens α. The counter is SNR: finer channels are noisier per channel, and whitney's CHIME is faint (peak ~0.2 vs noise ~0.05), so for *this* burst 16 may be near the SNR floor. For the **bright** bursts (casey, freya, zach, mahi) f_factor=64 is almost certainly leaving α-leverage on the table — 32 or even 16 (→64 ch) is affordable. The real defect is that it's a fixed 16 for everyone instead of SNR-tuned per burst.

**On the DSA window — also right, and it looks like the crop isn't firing.** on-pulse crop defaults ON (`FLITS_ONPULSE_CROP=1`) and the code comment claims "DSA crops to ~20 samples," but whitney's DSA still shows the full ~57 ms (1250 samples) for a ~0.1 ms burst. So either the crop is being skipped or its pad is swallowing the whole window. Tightening it cleans the noise estimate, the gain-solve conditioning, and χ² normalization.

**Honest limits (so I don't oversell):**
- Tighter DSA crop won't **un-rail whitney** — the railing is the broad-CHIME-vs-narrow-DSA tension under one τ∝ν^−α law, not a noise-window artifact.
- Cropping won't **create a 2nd DSA component** — time resolution is set by native sampling (t_factor=2), not the window. If a second DSA sub-pulse isn't resolved now, a tighter window won't reveal it; only finer t_factor would, if it's there.
- Finer CHIME channels mainly help the **bright** bursts; whitney itself is SNR-limited.

Concrete test I'd run: re-fit **whitney** (the failing case) + **zach** (bright control) with CHIME f_factor=16–32 and a forced-tight DSA crop, then compare α, per-band χ², and whether DSA conditioning improves. That isolates "is 16 channels hurting us" from "is whitney just a hard burst."

Want me to launch that 2-burst test, or apply the finer channelization campaign-wide and re-fit everything? The former is ~4 quick jobs and answers the methodology question; the latter is a full re-run of all 12 (and would supersede the α table).

169	    def _crop_on_pulse(self):
170	        """Crop the time axis to the burst + scattering tail + a noise margin.
171	
172	        Detects the on-pulse span as the contiguous-ish region where the smoothed
173	        band-integrated profile exceeds onpulse_thresh * sigma_offpulse (sigma from
174	        the outer-quarter MAD), then pads it by onpulse_pad_factor * span on each
175	        side. The pad leaves clean off-pulse for FRBModel._estimate_noise (which
176	        uses the cropped window's outer quarters) and absorbs the steep tail's
177	        approach to baseline. No-op (with a warning) if nothing clears threshold.
178	        """
179	        prof = np.nansum(self.data, axis=0)
180	        if self.smooth_ms > 0 and self.dt_ms > 0:
181	            prof = gaussian_filter1d(prof, sigma=(self.smooth_ms / 2.355) / self.dt_ms)
182	        n = prof.size
183	        q = max(n // 4, 1)
184	        base = np.r_[prof[:q], prof[-q:]]
185	        mu = np.median(base)
186	        sig = 1.4826 * np.median(np.abs(base - mu))
187	        if sig <= 0:
188	            log.warning(f"[{self.name}] on-pulse crop skipped: zero off-pulse spread")
189	            return
190	        on = np.where((prof - mu) > self.onpulse_thresh * sig)[0]
191	        if on.size == 0:
192	            log.warning(f"[{self.name}] on-pulse crop skipped: no samples above "
193	                        f"{self.onpulse_thresh}-sigma")
194	            return
195	        lo, hi = int(on.min()), int(on.max())
196	        span = hi - lo + 1
197	        pad = int(self.onpulse_pad_factor * span)
198	        lo2, hi2 = max(0, lo - pad), min(n, hi + pad + 1)
199	        self.data = self.data[:, lo2:hi2]
200	        self.time = np.arange(self.data.shape[1]) * self.dt_ms
201	        log.info(f"[{self.name}] on-pulse crop: {n} -> {self.data.shape[1]} samples "
202	                 f"(span {span}, pad {pad}); off-pulse fraction "
203	                 f"{1 - span / self.data.shape[1]:.2f}")
204

Verdict: **marginal raw speedup, real latency win — but the local `flits` env is missing `dynesty`** (the nested sampler), so it can't run the fit as-is.

- **Hardware:** 8 P-cores local vs 16 cluster cores — cluster has ~2× parallelism, Apple cores are faster each → roughly a wash for one fit. No big raw win.
- **Real win is latency:** no SLURM queue. This job sat pending a few min before running; local starts instantly.
- **Data's already local** ✓ (whitney CHIME+DSA .npy both present).
- **Blocker:** `dynesty` not installed in the local `flits` env (`pip install -e ".[nested]"` or `pip install dynesty` — one-time).

For **this** fit: not worth it — the cluster job is ~4 min in and nearly done; restarting locally would be slower. For the **iteration loop** (we'll likely retune whitney's crop/f_factor a few times), installing dynesty once and running single fits locally would kill the queue-wait and give instant turnaround on 8 P-cores.

The C2D1 figure is open for you. The verdict from it:

- **CHIME** (left) is now clean — finer 64-channel binning, model tracks it, χ²=1.11.

> AGENT

Native is 1024 (×32000 time); we're at 64 (f_factor=16). DSA native 6144 → 16.

There's no α benefit to 1024 and two real costs.

**Why no benefit:** α and τ are constrained by the *smooth* frequency evolution of the scattering tail, τ(ν)=τ₁GHz·ν⁻ᵅ. That's a slowly-varying function across 400–800 MHz. 64 channels = 6.25 MHz each already massively over-resolves it. 1024 channels carry the *same* information about α — just sliced thinner.

**Cost 1 — gain overfitting (the real one):** the likelihood marginalizes a *per-channel, per-component* gain (gₓ ~ N(0, s2)). So every channel you add is one more nuisance parameter per component. Going 64→1024 splits each channel's flux across 16, dropping per-channel SNR ~4×. Low-SNR channels give noisy gain estimates, and that estimation error leaks into the shared (τ, α) posterior. You spend 16× the degrees of freedom to absorb noise — it can *degrade* α, not sharpen it. It also makes χ²/pt and the gain reconstruction less trustworthy.

**Cost 2 — compute:** the ridge solve is per-channel × thousands of nested evals → roughly linear in channels. 1024 is ~16× slower (minutes → ~half hour locally) for no information gain.

**What actually sets the floor on channel width** (not raw resolution): keep channels narrow enough to (a) not average over the scintillation decorrelation bandwidth and (b) keep intra-channel DM smearing below the time resolution. For a CHIME-band FRB both sit in the ~64–256 zone, well short of 1024.

So 64 is near the sweet spot. The original whitney data was over-binned *below* that. If you want to confirm we're not under-resolving scint, the cheap test is run 128 or 256 and watch α/τ — if they don't move, channelization isn't the lever (the DSA second component is, which is what C2D2 is testing now).

whitney: **complete FAIL → PASS**. Validation against the 3-level contract:

- **L1** — converged (dlogz<0.5); τ=0.105 ms ✓; α=5.21 ± 0.2 **not railed** (floor 1.5 and ceiling 6.0 both ≳4σ away) ✓ → **PASS**

The mechanism, now proven: it was **prep, not the burst**. Default prep over-binned CHIME and buried the second DSA peak in a wide noise window → C2D1 forced one component across two peaks → α railed low (1.5). Finer CHIME + tight crop exposed both peaks → C2D2 unrails α to 5.21. logz +2722 over C2D1. No — it's steeper than Kolmogorov, and significantly so.

α = 5.21 +0.21/−0.18 vs Kolmogorov:
- vs **4.4** (thin-screen Kolmogorov, the repo's default): 0.81 high → **~4.6σ** above
- vs **4.0** (geometric/contract "near 4.0"): 1.21 high → **~6.9σ** above

So statistically inconsistent with Kolmogorov — a steeper-than-Kolmogorov index. Physically that points to anisotropic scattering, a steeper-than-Kolmogorov density spectrum / finite inner scale, or a single truncated screen.

One honest caveat: the ±0.2 is the **statistical** posterior width only. It does *not* fold in the prep systematics that drive this number — CHIME channelization, the 5σ crop threshold (could trim a faint DSA tail and bias α *high*), the C2D2 component choice, or cross-band DM alignment. Those are exactly what the pending fixed-s2 grid + a crop/channelization robustness sweep would pin down. So: confidently off-rail and steep, but I'd treat "5.21" as provisional until the systematics are bounded — the safe statement today is "whitney's α is steep, inconsistent with Kolmogorov," not the third digit.

For contrast, the Kolmogorov-consistent ones in the ladder are freya (4.36) and chromatica (3.29 is shallow); most of the sample sits *below* Kolmogorov.

> AGENT

Acronyms: PBF — Pulse-Broadening Function; EMG — Exponentially-Modified Gaussian.

Neither uniformly — it's **per-band**, and that's the default here. From the whitney log + `run_joint_fit.py:139-142`:

- **CHIME** = **power-law PBF**, β = 11/3 (Kolmogorov extended-medium broadening) → CHIME profile is Gaussian ⊛ power-law-PBF, *not* an EMG.
- **DSA** = **exponential PBF** → DSA is the classic thin-screen EMG (Gaussian ⊛ e^−t/τ).

So only DSA is the exp-modified Gaussian; CHIME carries a heavier power-law tail. The `b=3.67` in the log is β=11/3, the **density-spectrum** index — don't confuse it with the fitted α=5.21 (the τ∝ν⁻ᵅ scaling). For a Kolmogorov screen those are linked: α = 2β/(β−2) = 22/5 = **4.4**.

Two things follow, both important:

1. **The asymmetric PBF is a first-order systematic on α** — exactly the kind the ±0.2 doesn't capture. A power-law tail reaches a given CHIME broadening at a *smaller* characteristic τ than an exponential would, so CHIME-powerlaw + DSA-exp tends to push the lever-arm α **steep**. Part of why whitney lands at 5.21 rather than ~4.4 is plausibly this choice, not just the medium.

2. **The justification for the asymmetry is thin.** The comment (`:120-127`) is explicit: CHIME-powerlaw/DSA-exp beats all-exp by Δlnz=+4.0 **on wilhelm only**. It's the campaign default but not yet evidenced for whitney.

There's also a mild internal tension: the PBF *assumes* Kolmogorov β=11/3 (which implies α=4.4), yet the fitted α comes out 5.21 — steeper than the spectrum the kernel assumes.

Cheap, high-value check: rerun whitney C2D2 with `--pbf-C exp` (all-exponential). If α stays ~5 it's robust to PBF; if it drops toward 4.4 the steepness was the power-law tail. Want me to run it?

> DEVELOPER

but we can't have different PBFs between CHIME and DSA for the same burst --- it's the same burst!

> AGENT

You're right — same burst, same sightline, same scattering medium → the PBF *functional form* is fixed by the screen geometry; only its timescale τ scales with frequency. A power-law PBF at CHIME and an exponential at DSA is physically incoherent. The wilhelm Δlnz=+4.0 wasn't the medium changing shape between bands — it was the model using PBF freedom to absorb band-specific *profile* structure (the CHIME multi-peak), i.e. overfitting masquerading as physics.

And this is the default in the script (`--pbf-C powerlaw --pbf-D exp`), so **every** joint fit in the ladder inherited the mixed PBF. whitney first, then this needs flagging campaign-wide.

> AGENT

Found it — the "identical" was my own cp bug: my PBF-tracking edit landed *between* the two fits, so the powerlaw run auto-suffixed its output and my cp copied the stale exp file. The real powerlaw result was sitting under the auto-suffixed name. Corrected picture:

| PBF config | α | τ (ms) | logz | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| all-**exp** (thin screen) | **5.12** +0.17/−0.16 | 0.109 | 4997.3 | physical |
| all-**powerlaw** (Kolmogorov medium) | **1.51 RAILED** | 0.500 | 2288.9 | physical |
| mixed (pw/exp) | 5.21 | 0.105 | 5015.1 | unphysical |

So PBF is a **huge** knob, not negligible — powerlaw rails α to the floor. And the data decisively prefer **all-exponential**: Δlogz = **+2708** over powerlaw (clean Bayes factor, same data/dims). whitney's sightline is thin-screen-like.

Physical whitney answer: **α = 5.12 +0.17/−0.16** (all-exp). The headline survives — still steep, ~4.6σ above Kolmogorov. The unphysical mixed default happened to land α close (5.21), but that's luck: all-powerlaw shows the PBF can rail α entirely. The mixed default seeded the whole ladder, so the ladder needs an all-exp rerun.

Re-running all-exp with the fixed code now (clean metadata + independent reproduce of 5.12), then the figure:

> AGENT

**Does PBF only rail when it's power-law?**

No. Railing = the α posterior pinned to a prior edge, which happens whenever α is either *unconstrained* (no lever arm) or *forced to an extreme to absorb a model–data mismatch*. PBF shape is one such mismatch, not the only one. In this session:

- **PBF-induced** (whitney, correct prep + C2D2): all-powerlaw rails 1.51, all-exp doesn't (5.12). The sightline is thin-screen; a Kolmogorov power-law kernel (heavy tail, baked-in β=11/3≈α4.4) can't reproduce the sharp exponential DSA tail, so the fit flattens τ(ν) → rails α low.
- **Not PBF** — exp rails too when something else is wrong: whitney **C2D1 with exp DSA** railed 1.52 (wrong component count — one comp on two peaks); **hamilton** rails under every config because its DSA band is noise → no lever arm at all, PBF irrelevant.

So: power-law *can* rail a thin-screen sightline, but railing is the generic symptom of "model can't fit → α flees to the boundary." Exp is not immune. The discriminator is evidence + residuals, not the PBF family.

**Cluster mirror** — applied over SSH, verified by diff-against-backup (only the two intended edits) + AST parse; `.bak-pbf` saved. Both `run_joint_fit.py` copies now record PBF and auto-suffix non-default runs.

**PBF railing** — not exclusive to power-law. Railing is the generic "α flees to a prior edge when it's unconstrained or absorbing a misfit." Power-law railed whitney's thin-screen sightline; but exp railed it too at C2D1 (wrong component count), and hamilton rails under any PBF (DSA is noise, no lever arm). #!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=flits-joint
#SBATCH --partition=expansion
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
#SBATCH --mem=16G
#SBATCH --time=00:30:00
#SBATCH --output=/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs/logs/%x_%j.out
#SBATCH --error=/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs/logs/%x_%j.err
set -euo pipefail
BURST="${1:?pass a burst name}"
NLIVE="${2:-600}"
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=1
source /home/jfaber/flits/venv/bin/activate
cd /home/jfaber/flits/dsa110-FLITS/scattering
NPROC="${SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK:-8}"   # pool size tracks the core allocation
echo "[$(date)] node=$(hostname) joint burst=${BURST} nlive=${NLIVE} nproc=${NPROC} extra=${*:3}"
python -u /central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs/run_joint_fit.py "${BURST}" "${NLIVE}" "${NPROC}" "${@:3}"
echo "[$(date)] done rc=$?"
```

1	\section{Results}
2	\label{sec:results}
3	
4	\subsection{The per-sightline dispersion and scattering budget}
5	\label{sec:results-budget}
6	
7	Applying the decomposition of Section~\ref{sec:dm} (Eq.~\ref{eq:dmbudget}) to the
8	twelve sightlines yields the budget of Table~\ref{tab:budget} and
9	Figure~\ref{fig:budget}. The Galactic term is modest and similar across the
10	sample ($\mathrm{DM_{MW}}=78$--$171\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$), while the
11	cosmological mean grows with redshift to dominate the higher-$z$ sightlines. An
12	intervening circumgalactic column is significant only where a sightline passes
13	through a foreground galaxy's interior: three sightlines (FRB 20220310F, FRB 20230307A,
14	FRB 20230814A) fall in this galaxy-interior regime, where $\mathrm{DM_{int}}$ is
15	capped at $b=0.1\,R_{\mathrm{vir}}$ (the uncapped core-extrapolated columns reach
16	$364$--$712\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$), while most sightlines do not intersect a
17	confirmed foreground system and carry no intervening term. The host contribution
18	is the residual after the modeled terms are removed; for four sightlines (FRB 20220207C,
19	FRB 20220310F, FRB 20221203A, FRB 20230307A) it is formally negative---the modeled terms
20	over-predict $\mathrm{DM_{obs}}$. This is concentrated in the galaxy-interior
21	sightlines, where the capped circumgalactic column is most uncertain, and a
22	prior-predictive sensitivity analysis quantifies the probability of a negative
23	host term per sightline. Three sightlines (FRB 20230325A, FRB 20240122A, FRB 20230814A) lack a
24	spectroscopic host redshift and are carried only through the
25	redshift-independent Galactic term.
26	
27	The predicted intervening scattering spans
28	$\tau_{\mathrm{int}}\sim10^{-5}$--$1.4\,\mathrm{ms}$ at $1\,\mathrm{GHz}$, largest
29	for the galaxy-interior sightlines (Figure~\ref{fig:budget}, right). A direct
30	measured-versus-predicted comparison is not yet possible: of the three sightlines
31	with an attempted DSA scattering fit, all three fail the reduced-$\chi^2$ quality
32	gate, so no quality-passing measured $\tau$ is locked in and the scattering panel
33	is predicted-only. Closing this comparison requires quality-passing scattering
34	fits, which we identify as the principal remaining measurement for the sample.
35	
36	\input{budget_table.tex}
37	
38	\begin{figure*}
39	  \centering
40	  \includegraphics[width=0.95\textwidth]{sightline_dm_scattering_budget}
41	  \caption{Per-sightline dispersion and scattering budget for the twelve
42	  co-detections. \emph{Left:} the observed dispersion measure (black bar) of each
43	  burst decomposed into the Milky-Way ISM (NE2001) and halo, the cosmological mean
44	  (Macquart relation), the capped intervening circumgalactic column
45	  ($b<0.1\,R_{\mathrm{vir}}$), and the host residual; the placeholder-redshift
46	  sightlines (FRB 20230325A, FRB 20240122A, FRB 20230814A) show only the redshift-independent Galactic
47	  term. \emph{Right:} the predicted intervening pulse-broadening at $1\,\mathrm{GHz}$
48	  per sightline; the three sightlines with an attempted DSA scattering fit all
49	  fail the quality gate (``fit withheld''), so no measured $\tau$ is shown.
50	  Generated by the \texttt{dsa110-FLITS} pipeline
51	  (\texttt{galaxies/v2\_0/sightline\_budget.py}).}
52	  \label{fig:budget}
53	\end{figure*}
54	
55	\subsection{Scattering index and burst multiplicity}
56	\label{sec:results-alpha}
57	
58	% Demonstrated multi-component case = FRB 20220207C (internal nickname: zach).
59	% Numbers from the matched-normalization component grid.
60	A subset of our co-detected bursts is resolved into more than one temporal
61	component \citep{Pleunis2021}, and in these cases the inferred scattering index
62	depends on whether that multiplicity is modeled. We illustrate this with one co-detection whose
63	DSA-110 profile shows two sub-pulses while its CHIME/FRB profile presents a
64	single prominent peak yet fails the residual-whiteness gate. On the
65	matched-normalization grid, adding a second CHIME/FRB component is favored by
66	$\Delta\ln Z\approx+3.6\times10^{3}$ over the single-component model---roughly
67	forty times the evidence gain of adding a second DSA-110 component---and places
68	a broad companion $0.34$\,ms behind the main peak, blended beneath the
69	scattering tail where a simple peak search does not resolve it. Including this
70	component shifts the shared scattering index from $\alpha=3.32\pm0.01$ to
71	$\alpha=2.76\pm0.02$ and raises the scattering time from
72	$\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}}=0.42$ to $0.56$\,ms. The second DSA-110 sub-pulse, which
73	a single-band fit leaves pinned at the minimum-separation prior bound, relocates
74	to its observed delay only once the CHIME/FRB component constrains the shared
75	$(\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}},\alpha)$: the two bands are coupled through one
76	scattering law.
77	
78	\subsection{Isotropic-equivalent energies}
79	\label{sec:burst-energies}
80	
81	For each sightline with a spectroscopic host redshift we estimate the
82	isotropic-equivalent burst energy directly from the joint CHIME--DSA fit,
83	without extrapolating either band's spectrum beyond where it is constrained.
84	The joint fit returns a per-band spectral amplitude and index,
85	$F_X(\nu) = c_{0,X}\,(\nu/\nu_{\mathrm{ref},X})^{\gamma_X}$, which we place on an
86	absolute scale with each telescope's per-channel radiometer conversion
87	$\sigma_{S,X}(\nu) = \mathrm{SEFD}_X(\nu)\,/\,[\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{pol}}\,\Delta\nu\,\Delta t}\,G_X(\nu)]$,
88	taking the system-equivalent flux density and primary-beam gain $G_X$ from the
89	DSA-110 \citep{Law2024} and CHIME/FRB \citep{CHIMEFRB2018,Michilli2021} flux
90	scales, and integrate over each instrument's observing band---CHIME over
91	$0.400$--$0.800\,\mathrm{GHz}$ and DSA over $1.311$--$1.499\,\mathrm{GHz}$,
92	%
93	\begin{equation}
94	E_{\mathrm{iso}} = \frac{4\pi D_L^2(z)}{1+z}\left[
95	  \int_{\nu_1^{C}}^{\nu_2^{C}} s_C\,F_{\mathrm{CHIME}}(\nu)\,d\nu
96	  + \int_{\nu_1^{D}}^{\nu_2^{D}} s_D\,F_{\mathrm{DSA}}(\nu)\,d\nu
97	\right],
98	\label{eq:eiso}
99	\end{equation}
100	%
101	with $D_L(z)$ from the fiducial \textit{Planck}\,2018 cosmology
102	\citep{Planck2018}, the $(1+z)$ bandwidth k-correction applied, and
103	$1\,\mathrm{Jy\,ms\,Hz} = 10^{-29}\,\mathrm{J\,m^{-2}}$. Bursts whose hosts lack
104	a spectroscopic redshift are omitted. This band-restricted integral constrains
105	the energy released \emph{within the observed spectral envelope}: it avoids the
106	large, model-dependent extrapolation that a single power-law fit across the full
107	$0.4$--$1.5\,\mathrm{GHz}$ span would require, at the cost of not counting flux in
108	the unobserved $0.8$--$1.3\,\mathrm{GHz}$ gap, so the tabulated values are lower
109	limits on the total $0.4$--$1.5\,\mathrm{GHz}$ energy
110	(Table~\ref{tab:burst-energies}). The most distant sightline, FRB 20221203A
111	($z=0.51$), reaches $E_{\mathrm{iso}}\simeq1.1\times10^{41}\,\mathrm{erg}$, at the
112	luminous end of the co-detected sample. The absolute flux scale is anchored to
113	the DSA-110 catalog \citep{Law2024} for the three sightlines with a published
114	catalog fluence (FRB 20220506D, FRB 20220310F, FRB 20220207C), which reproduce the catalog values to
115	within a factor of two; the remaining bands rely on the radiometer model without
116	an independent catalog cross-check, so their energies carry the additional,
117	unquantified systematic of the absolute scale.
118

123	band's radiometer flux calibration. $\gamma_C,\gamma_D$ are the per-band spectral

2	\label{sec:discussion}
3	
4	% TODO: the coherent-picture cases — an intersecting foreground galaxy near the

10	\subsection{Burst multiplicity as a systematic on the scattering index}
11	\label{sec:disc-alpha}
12	
13	The result of Section~\ref{sec:results-alpha} is a cautionary systematic for any
14	single-component scattering index. A temporal sub-component omitted from the
15	model is partially absorbed into the scattering tail, biasing $\alpha$ high: in
16	the case we examined the bias is $\Delta\alpha\approx0.56$, many times the formal
17	uncertainty. Because $\alpha$ is the quantity that distinguishes a Kolmogorov
18	turbulent screen ($\alpha\simeq4.4$; \citealp{Rickett1990}) from a shallower
19	spectrum, an unrecognized companion can masquerade as anomalous,
20	sub-Kolmogorov scattering---a regime in which measured pulse-broadening indices
21	already scatter well below the Kolmogorov value
22	\citep{Bhat2004}. We verified
23	that the favored second component is not an artifact of the likelihood:
24	reconstructing the single-component residual reproduces the whiteness statistic
25	that flagged the burst, the evidence gain is free of the eigenvalue-conditioning
26	pathology that a spurious near-degenerate component would trigger, and the
27	companion sits well inside the resolvable separation. Even the two-component
28	model, however, does not fully whiten the residual---a sharp rising edge
29	survives, consistent with an intrinsic fast rise, a limitation of the
30	scattered-pulse kernel, or a third component---so the corrected $\alpha$ should
31	be read as better-conditioned rather than final. A systematic re-fit of the
32	flagged co-detections in our sample is underway.
33

1	\section{Observations and Sample}
2	\label{sec:obs}
3	
4	Our sample is the twelve fast radio bursts detected simultaneously by CHIME/FRB
5	\citep{CHIMEFRB2018} at $0.4$--$0.8$\,GHz and by DSA-110 \citep{Law2024} at
6	$\sim$1.4\,GHz between 2022 February and 2024 February (MJD $59617$--$60369$).
7	The defining asset of the sample is that each burst is seen twice across a
8	$\sim$1\,GHz frequency baseline, which---as developed in
9	Section~\ref{sec:jointfit}---breaks the degeneracy between the scattering time
10	and its spectral index that defeats any single-band fit. The bursts span a
11	dispersion measure range of $262$--$960$\,pc\,cm$^{-3}$; their nicknames, TNS
12	designations, epochs, widths, and time-of-arrival residuals are listed in
13	Table~\ref{tab:toa}. We report all twelve, noting per sightline the level at
14	which each quantity is constrained rather than imposing a single detection
15	threshold.
16	
17	\subsection{Dynamic spectra and reduction}
18	\label{sec:data}
19	
20	For each co-detection we analyze a pair of total-intensity dynamic spectra---one
21	per facility---derived from the CHIME/FRB and DSA-110 baseband recordings
22	(24 spectra in total; provenance and array geometry in
23	\texttt{DATA\_SOURCES.md} of the companion \texttt{dsa110-FLITS} archive). Each
24	spectrum is loaded with its frequency axis standardized to ascending order and
25	its per-channel bandpass normalized, so the fitted amplitudes are free of the
26	band-edge rolloff. All fits, quality gates, and figures in this paper are
27	produced by the open \texttt{dsa110-FLITS} pipeline (\texttt{pipeline/}), which
28	we reference throughout for reproducibility. We do not catalog the fine
29	baseband morphology of each burst here; the only morphological distinction the
30	analysis depends on---whether a burst resolves into more than one temporal
31	component---is treated where it matters, in the multi-component fit of
32	Section~\ref{sec:multicomp}.
33	
34	\subsection{DSA-110 scattering fits}
35	\label{sec:obs-scatt}
36	
37	The joint CHIME--DSA fit yields a $1.4$\,GHz pulse-broadening time
38	$\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}}$ wherever a scattering tail is resolved, measured against
39	the NE2001 Galactic prediction along the sightline. Only three sightlines
40	(FRB 20221203A, FRB 20230325A, FRB 20240229A) currently have an attempted scattering fit, and all three
41	fail the reduced-$\chi^2$ quality gate; their scattering times are therefore
42	withheld, and no quality-passing measured $\tau$ is locked in for any sightline.
43	The remaining nine sightlines have no scattering fit on record. The predicted
44	intervening contribution along every sightline---the quantity we can compute
45	without a measurement---is presented in Section~\ref{sec:budget} and
46	Figure~\ref{fig:budget}; closing the measured-versus-predicted comparison awaits
47	quality-passing fits, which we identify as the principal remaining measurement
48	for the sample.
49	
50	\subsection{Foreground-galaxy search}
51	\label{sec:obs-fg}
52	
53	To establish which sightlines could carry an intervening dispersion or
54	scattering contribution, we searched each of the twelve fields for foreground
55	galaxies and clusters, cross-matching candidates against the DESI Legacy Imaging
56	Survey DR9 with \citet{Zhou2021} photometric redshifts, DESI DR1 spectroscopic
57	redshifts, the NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database, and PS1-STRM \citep{Beck2021}.
58	The search returns 49 candidate systems---34 galaxy halos and 15 clusters---along
59	nine of the twelve sightlines (three fields yield no candidate). For each
60	candidate we record the proper impact parameter (12--280\,kpc for the halos;
61	clusters by $b/R_{500}$) and the best available redshift and its provenance
62	(spectroscopic or photometric); the full catalog is Table~\ref{tab:foreground}.
63	Spectroscopic host redshifts are available for nine of the twelve bursts
64	($z=0.043$--$0.51$), while three (FRB 20230325A, FRB 20240122A, FRB 20230814A) carry only a
65	placeholder redshift and are excluded from any distance-dependent quantity. We measure no host stellar masses; the only masses entering the
66	analysis are the halo-mass proxies of the intervening systems used by the
67	circumgalactic dispersion model (Section~\ref{sec:dm}), whose confidence we flag
68	per system. The verdict logic that classifies each candidate as foreground,
69	background, or inconclusive, and the resulting dispersion budget, follow in
70	Section~\ref{sec:budget}.
71	
72	\input{sections/toa.tex}
73
