1	\section{The Dispersion and Scattering Budget}
2	\label{sec:budget}
3	
4	% Core methods section. The observed DM decomposes as
5	%   DM_obs = DM_MW,ISM + DM_MW,halo + <DM_cosmic>(z) + DM_intervening + DM_host,
6	% with DM_MW,ISM from NE2001/YMW16 (pygedm), DM_MW,halo a 40 pc/cm^3 prior
7	% (Yamasaki & Totani 2020), <DM_cosmic>(z) the Macquart relation
8	% (Macquart et al. 2020; f_IGM=0.84, chi_e=0.875), and DM_intervening a two-phase
9	% (hot mNFW + clumpy cool) CGM column for each intersecting foreground galaxy,
10	% reported raw and capped at b = 0.1 R_vir (the galaxy-interior regime).
11	%
12	% Scattering: measured tau_1GHz from nested-sampling fits (quality-gated on
13	% reduced chi^2, with R^2/normality informational only), compared against the
14	% predicted intervening tau from a thin-screen two-phase model.
15	
16	\subsection{Dispersion Measure Decomposition}
17	\label{sec:dm}
18	
19	The observed dispersion measure of each co-detection separates into Galactic,
20	cosmological, host, and (where the sightline intersects a foreground galaxy)
21	intervening contributions \citep{CordesChatterjee2019},
22	\begin{equation}
23	\mathrm{DM_{obs}} = \mathrm{DM_{MW}} + \langle\mathrm{DM_{cosmic}}\rangle(z)
24	+ \mathrm{DM_{int}} + \mathrm{DM_{host}},
25	\label{eq:dmbudget}
26	\end{equation}
27	with the Galactic term $\mathrm{DM_{MW}} = \mathrm{DM_{MW,ISM}} +
28	\mathrm{DM_{MW,halo}}$ split between disk and halo. We estimate the disk
29	contribution $\mathrm{DM_{MW,ISM}}$ from the NE2001 \citep{CordesLazio2002} and
30	YMW16 \citep{YMW2017} electron-density models and adopt a
31	$\sim$40\,pc\,cm$^{-3}$ Milky-Way halo prior \citep{YamasakiTotani2020}. The
32	cosmological mean $\langle\mathrm{DM_{cosmic}}\rangle(z)$ follows the Macquart
33	relation \citep{Macquart2020}. For the sightlines that cross a foreground
34	galaxy we model the intervening circumgalactic column $\mathrm{DM_{int}}$ as a
35	two-phase (hot modified-NFW plus clumpy cool) medium, taking the mNFW gas
36	profile from \citet{ProchaskaZheng2019}. Such intervening halos can imprint
37	measurable dispersion and, where the gas is turbulent, scattering on FRB
38	sightlines \citep{Ocker2021}, although an individual quiescent halo may instead
39	yield only an upper limit on its scattering contribution \citep{Prochaska2019}.
40	The residual after the modeled terms are removed is attributed to the host.
41	
42	\subsection{Intervening Foreground Galaxies and Clusters}
43	\label{sec:foreground}
44	
45	The intervening term $\mathrm{DM_{int}}$ is sourced only where a sightline
46	actually intersects foreground circumgalactic or intracluster gas, so we first
47	establish which candidate systems along the twelve sightlines are genuinely in
48	the foreground. Each candidate is cross-matched against the DESI Legacy Imaging
49	Survey DR9 with \citet{Zhou2021} photometric redshifts, DESI DR1 spectroscopic
50	redshifts, the NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database (NED), and PS1-STRM
51	\citep{Beck2021}---by coordinate match (morphology and redshift) and, for the
52	PS1-classified halos, by direct \texttt{objID} lookup. We label a candidate
53	\emph{confirmed} foreground when its best catalog redshift lies below the FRB
54	host redshift, \emph{background} when at or above it, and \emph{inconclusive}
55	when the redshift straddles the host within $1\sigma$, the host lacks a
56	spectroscopic redshift, or no trustworthy redshift exists (a PS1-STRM
57	\texttt{UNSURE} classification or extrapolated photo-$z$). Of the 49 candidates
58	in Table~\ref{tab:foreground}, 29 are confirmed foreground, 7 are background,
59	and 13 remain inconclusive; the photometric redshifts in the source compilation
60	are superseded by the catalog values reported here. Only one of the 15 clusters
61	has an impact parameter inside its own $R_{500}$, so for the rest the sightline
62	does not pierce the intracluster medium and the cluster contributes negligibly
63	to $\mathrm{DM_{int}}$.
64	
65	\input{foreground_table.tex}
66	
67	\subsection{Scattering Attribution}
68	\label{sec:scattering}
69	
70	We measure the pulse-broadening time and its frequency scaling from the
71	co-detected dynamic spectra and compare them against the scattering predicted
72	by each candidate screen: the Milky-Way ISM, an intervening circumgalactic
73	medium, or a host galaxy, where the host can dominate the scattering of a
74	heavily broadened burst \citep{Ocker2022}. The fits are produced by the
75	\texttt{dsa110-FLITS} pipeline (\texttt{pipeline/}).
76	
77	\begin{figure}
78	  \centering
79	  \includegraphics[width=0.95\columnwidth]{wilhelm_scint_dnud_ne2025}
80	  \caption{Scintillation decorrelation bandwidth $\Delta\nu_d$ versus frequency for
81	  FRB~20221203A. DSA-resolved $\Delta\nu_d\approx0.13$\,MHz (blue; nearly flat,
82	  $x=-0.23\pm0.19$ over the 10\% DSA lever arm); CHIME upper limits (red) since the
83	  diffractive scale is sub-channel at native resolution. Purple stars: the NE2025
84	  Milky-Way scattering floor, $\sim8\times$ \emph{above} the measurement. Green
85	  dash-dot: the pulse-broadening screen ($2\pi\tau\,\Delta\nu_d=C_1=1$), $\sim85\times$
86	  \emph{below}. The three separated scales imply the dominant pulse-broadening screen
87	  is neither the Galactic floor nor the resolved scintillation screen (a strong
88	  host/intervening screen). NE2025 Galactic electron-density model from
89	  \citet{Ocker2026}.}
90	  \label{fig:scint_screens}
91	\end{figure}
92	
93	\begin{figure}
94	  \centering
95	  \includegraphics[width=0.95\columnwidth]{codetection_scint_excess}
96	  \caption{Is the FRB 20221203A scattering excess sightline-specific or systematic?
97	  Scattering excess (NE2025 Milky-Way-floor $\Delta\nu_d$ divided by the measured
98	  DSA diffractive $\Delta\nu_d$; excess${=}1$ is the MW floor, dashed) versus
99	  Galactic latitude $|b|$ for the 12 CHIME--DSA co-detections. Error bars combine
100	  the measurement error with NE2025's floor uncertainty ($\sigma\approx0.4$\,dex,
101	  $\sim\!\times2.5$); the annotated $z$ is the significance above the MW floor.
102	  $\Delta\nu_d$ is the narrowest consistent cluster of well-constrained
103	  Lorentzian/Gen-Lorentz widths across all stored per-subband scintillation fits
104	  (rejecting fits railed at the $0.060$\,MHz bound). Filled circles: cleanly-resolved
105	  diffractive scales significant at $z>2$ -- FRB 20220207C ($10.7\times$), FRB 20221203A
106	  ($8.0\times$), FRB 20230913A ($7.2\times$), all in the shaded band. Open circle: FRB 20240229A
107	  ($9.6\times$, single-subband, low confidence). Light-blue: clean but $z<2$
108	  (FRB 20240203A $5.9\times$, FRB 20220506D $2.6\times$). Orange up-triangles: lower limits
109	  (single-component or rail-only fits). The grey band ($|b|<14^\circ$) marks
110	  sightlines where NE2025 intersects voids and the floor is unreliable (FRB 20230814A,
111	  FRB 20221113A, FRB 20240122A fall below unity there). The excess clusters at $\sim7$--$11\times$ on
112	  $3$--$4$ independent mid-$|b|$ sightlines where the floor is reliable and the
113	  diffractive scale resolvable (three high-confidence: FRB 20220207C, FRB 20221203A, FRB 20230913A;
114	  FRB 20240229A adds a fourth at high $|b|$ but is low-confidence), and never the reverse --
115	  evidence for a common (host/intervening) scattering enhancement rather than a
116	  FRB 20221203A-only peculiarity. Per-sightline significance is $\sim\!2\sigma$, dominated
117	  by NE2025's floor uncertainty; because that error is a shared systematic across
118	  sightlines (not independent), the result rests on the \emph{asymmetry} -- the
119	  measurement is always in excess where the floor is reliable, never below -- rather
120	  than on a stacked significance. NE2025 Galactic electron-density model from
121	  \citet{Ocker2026}.}
122	  \label{fig:codetection_excess}
123	\end{figure}
124	
125	Figure~\ref{fig:scint_screens} shows the three separated scattering scales for the
126	prototype sightline FRB~20221203A, and Figure~\ref{fig:codetection_excess} extends the
127	Milky-Way-floor comparison to all twelve co-detections. The diffractive-scintillation
128	excess relative to the modeled Milky-Way floor is robust to the choice of Galactic
129	electron-density model among the scattering-calibrated models of the same lineage:
130	NE2025 \citep{Ocker2026} yields an excess on all six mid-latitude sightlines
131	($2.6$--$10.7\times$) and NE2001 \citep{CordesLazio2002} confirms it ($6/6$,
132	$2.2$--$7.3\times$), while YMW16 \citep{YMW2017} reverses it, predicting a floor below the
133	measured value on five of the six. We attribute this reversal to YMW16's per-sightline
134	scattering unreliability rather than to an absence of excess: by construction YMW16
135	incorporates no interstellar-scattering data and derives $\tau$ from an empirical
136	$\tau$--$\mathrm{DM}$ relation with $\sim\!1$\,dex scatter, whereas NE2025 and NE2001
137	forward-model scattering from the electron-density-fluctuation field. Because the adopted
138	NE2025 floor itself carries a factor $\sim\!2$--$3$ per-sightline uncertainty that acts as a
139	systematic shared across sightlines---and therefore does not average down as $\sqrt{N}$---we
140	regard only the high-amplitude sightlines ($\sim\!7$--$11\times$) as robust evidence for an
141	extragalactic scattering screen, with the lowest-amplitude cases ($\sim\!2.6$--$3\times$)
142	remaining consistent with the floor uncertainty.
143	
144	\subsubsection{The joint two-band fit}
145	\label{sec:jointfit}
146	
147	A single-band scattering fit cannot separate the scattering index $\alpha$ from
148	the scattering time, because the pulse broadening
149	$\tau(\nu)=\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}}\,(\nu/1\,\mathrm{GHz})^{-\alpha}$ enters a
150	single band only through its value at that band's frequency: one band fixes the
151	product, not the slope. Co-detection breaks this degeneracy. We fit the
152	CHIME/FRB ($\sim$0.4--0.8\,GHz) and DSA-110 ($\sim$1.4\,GHz) dynamic spectra
153	\emph{simultaneously} with a shared sightline pair
154	$(\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}},\alpha)$ and per-telescope pulse parameters (arrival
155	time $t_0$, intrinsic width $\zeta$, and a residual dispersion
156	$\delta\mathrm{DM}$). The $\sim$1\,GHz lever arm between the bands measures
157	$\alpha$ directly: the ratio of the two scattering times pins the slope, while
158	the shared normalization $\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}}$ pins its value at 1\,GHz. With
159	$\alpha$ held at the Kolmogorov value $4.4$ \citep{Rickett1990}, the two bands
160	instead return $\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}}$ estimates that disagree by up to an
161	order of magnitude for the same sightline---evidence that $\alpha\neq4.4$ along
162	these lines of sight.
163	
164	\begin{figure}
165	  \centering
166	  \includegraphics[width=0.95\columnwidth]{pbf_shapes}
167	  \caption{Pulse-broadening function (PBF) shapes used in the joint fit. A Gaussian
168	  intrinsic pulse convolved with a thin-screen exponential PBF (green) versus
169	  power-law-spectrum PBFs with density index $\beta=3.00$ and $\beta=11/3$
170	  (Kolmogorov). Smaller $\beta$ yields a heavier $t^{-\beta/2}$ tail; $\beta\to4$
171	  recovers the exponential \citep[\S11.2]{Cordes2025}.}
172	  \label{fig:pbf_shapes}
173	\end{figure}
174	
175	\begin{figure*}
176	  \centering
177	  \includegraphics[width=0.95\textwidth]{wilhelm_pbf_evidence}
178	  \caption{Band-dependent PBF preference for FRB~20221203A. \emph{Left:} change in
179	  log-evidence relative to the exponential PBF versus power-law index $\beta$ (best
180	  single-component, per band). CHIME (400--800\,MHz) mildly prefers a Kolmogorov
181	  tail ($\Delta\ln Z=+6.2$ at $\beta=11/3$); DSA (1.2--1.5\,GHz) rejects
182	  heavier-than-exponential tails monotonically. \emph{Right:} joint CHIME+DSA
183	  evidence (C1D1). A \emph{per-band} PBF (CHIME power-law, DSA exponential) beats the
184	  all-exponential model by $\Delta\ln Z=+4.0$ ($\sim6\sigma$), whereas a global
185	  power-law loses $84$. The two bands require different PBFs.}
186	  \label{fig:pbf_evidence}
187	\end{figure*}
188	
189	\subsubsection{Gain-marginalized likelihood}
190	\label{sec:gainmarg}
191	
192	The per-channel amplitude of an FRB spectrum is unknown and strongly modulated
193	by scintillation; carried as a free spectral envelope it leaves correlated
194	structure in the fit residuals and invalidates a $\chi^2$ goodness-of-fit test.
195	We therefore marginalize the per-channel gain analytically. With a Gaussian
196	prior on the gain the per-channel evidence is available in closed form (a
197	matched-filter likelihood), and the recovered gain absorbs both the burst
198	spectrum and the scintillation pattern. This removes the spectral and
199	scintillation structure from the residual, so that the reduced $\chi^2$ and the
200	lag-1 residual autocorrelation become meaningful quality gates, and it lowers
201	the sampled dimensionality. We
202	sample the posterior by nested sampling \citep{Skilling2004}, as implemented in
203	\texttt{dynesty} \citep{Speagle2020}, and quality-gate each fit on its reduced
204	$\chi^2$ and residual whiteness, treating $R^2$ and residual normality as
205	informational.
206	
207	\subsubsection{Multiple temporal components}
208	\label{sec:multicomp}
209	
210	Some bursts comprise more than one temporal sub-component, a common feature of
211	the resolved FRB population \citep{Hessels2019, Pleunis2021}. An unmodeled
212	second component is partially absorbed by a single scattered pulse---as a steeper slope
213	and a larger scattering time---and so biases the inferred $\alpha$. We extend
214	the likelihood to $N$ temporal components per band, each contributing its own
215	$(t_0,\zeta)$ while $(\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}},\alpha)$ remain shared across both
216	bands and all components, and we select the number of components per band by
217	Bayesian evidence. Because the evidence normalization differs between likelihood
218	variants, the component counts are compared on a single matched grid in which
219	even the one-component model is evaluated through the multi-component
220	likelihood, so that evidence differences are meaningful. Component arrival times
221	within a band are ordered and separated by a data-derived minimum spacing,
222	keeping the fit identifiable at every prior sample. A clean single-component
223	co-detection in our sample, for which the joint fit returns
224	$\alpha=4.48\pm0.04$ with white residuals, validates the method; a
225	multi-component case is presented in Section~\ref{sec:results-alpha}.
226	% Validating clean case = burst internally labelled "FRB 20230325A" (swap to TNS name).
227

  "new_string": "The dispersion measure (DM) of a fast radio burst (FRB) is an integral of free\nelectrons along the line of sight, and as such a sum of contributions from\nphysically distinct media: the Milky-Way interstellar medium and halo, the\nintergalactic medium whose mean grows with redshift through the Macquart\nrelation \\citep{Macquart2020}, the circumgalactic medium of any intervening\ngalaxy the sightline pierces, and the FRB's host galaxy\n\\citep{CordesChatterjee2019}. The cosmological term makes the FRB DM a baryon\nprobe, but only once the foreground and host contributions are separated;\nconversely, an intervening galaxy's circumgalactic column is itself a probe of\ncool halo gas, accessible only where it can be isolated from the other terms.\n\nScattering carries complementary information. Multipath propagation through\nturbulent ionized gas broadens the pulse by a time\n$\\tau(\\nu)=\\tau_{1\\,\\mathrm{GHz}}\\,(\\nu/1\\,\\mathrm{GHz})^{-\\alpha}$, whose\nspectral index $\\alpha$ encodes the turbulent density spectrum and the\nscattering geometry: a Kolmogorov thin screen predicts $\\alpha\\simeq4.4$\n\\citep{Rickett1990}, while measured pulse-broadening indices frequently fall\nbelow this value \\citep{Bhat2004}. Because $\\tau$ and $\\alpha$ enter a single\nobserving band only through the broadening at that band's frequency, a\nsingle-band measurement cannot separate them: the same data are reproduced by a\nlarge $\\tau$ with a steep index or a small $\\tau$ with a shallow one.\n\nSimultaneous detection across a wide frequency baseline breaks this degeneracy.\nThe twelve FRBs studied here were each recorded by both CHIME/FRB at\n$0.4$--$0.8$\\,GHz \\citep{CHIMEFRB2018} and DSA-110 at $\\sim$1.4\\,GHz\n\\citep{Law2024}, a $\\sim$1\\,GHz lever arm over which the ratio of the two\nscattering times fixes $\\alpha$ directly. We use this leverage to ask, sightline\nby sightline, which medium contributes which observed feature---decomposing each\nburst's DM into its Galactic, cosmological, intervening, and host terms\n(Section~\\ref{sec:budget}), attributing its scattering to a Galactic,\nintervening, or host screen (Section~\\ref{sec:scattering}), and measuring the\nshared $(\\tau_{1\\,\\mathrm{GHz}},\\alpha)$ with a joint two-band fit\n(Section~\\ref{sec:jointfit}). Section~\\ref{sec:obs} describes the sample,\nSection~\\ref{sec:results} presents the per-sightline budget and the\nisotropic-equivalent energies, and Sections~\\ref{sec:discussion}--%\n\\ref{sec:conclusions} discuss the cases where an intervening galaxy is the likely\nscattering screen and what co-detection adds."

{
  "file_path": "/Users/jakobfaber/Developer/repos/github.com/jakobtfaber/dsa110-FLITS/analysis/scattering-refit-2026-06/joint_ladder/ALLEXP_PBF_RUN.md",
  "content": "# All-exponential PBF ladder rerun — HPCC campaign (2026-06-24)\n\nPBF = pulse-broadening function; lnZ = log Bayesian evidence.\n\n## Purpose\n\nEvery joint CHIME–DSA fit in the original ladder used the `run_joint_fit.py`\ndefault of a **mixed** PBF — `--pbf-C powerlaw --pbf-D exp` (CHIME a Kolmogorov\npower-law tail, DSA an exponential). That default is physically incoherent: a\nsingle burst on a single sightline sees one scattering medium, so the PBF\n*functional form* is fixed by the screen geometry and only its timescale τ scales\nwith frequency. A power-law tail at CHIME and an exponential at DSA cannot both\ndescribe the same screen. The per-band preference that motivated the default\n(wilhelm, ΔlnZ ≈ +4.0 for per-band over all-exponential) is the model using PBF\nshape freedom to absorb band-specific *profile* structure — overfitting, not\nmedium physics.\n\nThis run re-fits the whole ladder under the **physical all-exponential PBF**\n(`--pbf-C exp --pbf-D exp`), changing only the PBF and holding each burst's\nbest-model configuration, α-prior, and gain treatment fixed, so that\nα_exp − α_mixed isolates the PBF systematic per burst.\n\n## Design and provenance\n\n- **Driver:** dynamic workflow `allexp-ladder` (run `wf_4b71052d-9b7`; 17 agents,\n  ~33 min wall) — Submit → Drain (poll `squeue`) → per-burst Verify → Synthesize.\n- **Compute:** Caltech HPCC, `partition=expansion`, via\n  `/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs/run_joint.sbatch` (8 cores, 16 GB,\n  30 min default).\n- **Per-burst command** (model flags from each burst's ladder best-model;\n  α-bounds [1.5, 6.0] throughout):\n\n  ```\n  sbatch run_joint.sbatch <burst> 600 <model-flags> \\\n         --alpha-lo 1.5 --alpha-hi 6.0 --pbf-C exp --pbf-D exp\n  ```\n\n  sharedzeta bursts (`--shared-zeta`): freya, casey, chromatica, wilhelm,\n  hamilton. Component bursts (`--marginalize-gain --components-C X\n  --components-D Y`): mahi (C1D1 `--force-multi`), phineas (C3D3), oran (C2D1),\n  isha (C2D1), zach (C2D3), johndoeII (C2D1). whitney was done separately on the\n  local machine (C2D2, re-prepped) and is folded in for completeness.\n- **Output naming:** the PBF-tracking edit (this session) records\n  `pbf_C/pbf_D/beta_C/beta_D` in each JSON and auto-suffixes non-default PBF runs,\n  so all outputs land as `<burst>_joint_fit_<tag>_pbf-exp-exp.json` with no\n  clobber of the mixed-default files. Verdicts computed by\n  `/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs/_allexp_verify.py` and independently\n  re-checked from the JSONs (10/10 α match).\n\n## Results\n\nα_mixed is the original mixed-PBF ladder value; α_exp is this run. \"railed/wide\"\nflags a posterior whose median sits within 3σ of a prior bound (1.5 or 6.0) —\neither a hard pin or a wide tail that reaches the bound.\n\n| burst | α_mixed | α_exp (all-exp) | Δα | railed/wide | status |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| whitney | 5.21 | 5.12 | −0.09 | no | done (local, C2D2, re-prep) |\n| isha | 5.39 | 5.48 +0.42/−1.98 | +0.09 | wide → upper | done |\n| freya | 4.36 | 4.356 ± 0.04 | −0.004 | no | done |\n| phineas | 3.33 | *pending* | — | — | RUNNING (job 64538743) |\n| chromatica | 3.28 | 3.286 ± ~0.04 | +0.006 | no | done |\n| mahi | 3.80 | 3.17 +1.47/−1.18 | **−0.63** | wide → floor | done |\n| oran | 2.69 | 2.662 ± 0.16 | −0.028 | no | done |\n| wilhelm | 2.56 | 2.558 ± ~0.04 | −0.002 | no | done |\n| zach | 2.41 | *pending* | — | — | RUNNING (job 64538745) |\n| casey | 2.40 | 2.396 ± ~0.04 | −0.004 | no | done |\n| johndoeII | 1.58 | 1.573 (≈floor) | −0.007 | railed (floor) | done |\n| hamilton | 1.50 | 1.504 (≈floor) | +0.004 | railed (floor) | done |\n\n(lnZ is not tabulated here: the sharedzeta and component likelihoods sit on\ndifferent normalizations, so lnZ is comparable only exp-vs-mixed *within* a burst,\nnot across the column.)\n\n## Interpretation\n\n1. **The PBF systematic is small for the well-constrained bursts.** The six\n   un-railed bursts — freya, casey, chromatica, wilhelm, oran, and whitney — move\n   by |Δα| ≤ 0.09 between the mixed and physical PBF. Their published α are\n   *confirmed, not overturned*; the all-exp values agree and become canonical for\n   physical consistency.\n2. **The per-band PBF was immaterial to the science.** wilhelm — the burst whose\n   +4.0 evidence justified the mixed default — has α 2.56 → 2.558 under all-exp.\n   The per-band PBF should be dropped: it neither changes a result nor reflects a\n   physical screen.\n3. **mahi is a new concern.** Under all-exp its α falls 3.80 → 3.17 and the\n   posterior widens to +1.47/−1.18, reaching the prior floor. mahi's α is\n   PBF-sensitive and poorly constrained once the unphysical CHIME power-law tail\n   is removed; it needs a re-prep / model re-check (as whitney did), not a simple\n   value swap.\n4. **isha, johndoeII, hamilton are unconstrained under either PBF.** isha rails\n   the upper bound with a wide lower tail; johndoeII and hamilton are hard-pinned\n   at the 1.5 floor. No PBF choice rescues them.\n\n## Outstanding\n\n- **phineas (C3D3) and zach (C2D3) timed out** in the first round (jobs\n  64537453/456, TIMEOUT at the 30-min wall — the 6-component fits are the slowest)\n  and were resubmitted at **2 h / 16 cores** (jobs **64538743 / 64538745**, both\n  RUNNING as of this writing). zach is the marquee profile-bias case (mixed-PBF\n  3.32 → 2.41), so its all-exp value must complete before any ladder publication\n  claim. Poller `bqyjvqea6` is watching for drain.\n- On completion, the all-exp α for the six well-constrained bursts become the\n  canonical ladder values, and the manuscript's PBF section\n  (`fig:pbf_evidence`, §jointfit \"the two bands require different PBFs\") is revised\n  to drop the per-band PBF as unphysical-and-immaterial.\n\n## Verdict\n\nThe mixed-PBF ladder α are trustworthy **only for the six un-railed bursts**, and\nfor those the physical all-exp PBF confirms them. The six others —\nmahi, isha, johndoeII, hamilton (railed/wide) and phineas, zach (pending) — block\npublishing the ladder as-is.\n"
}
